messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [redacted]
Medical Record Number: [redacted]
Date of Admission: [redacted]
Date of Discharge: [redacted]
Final Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The patient, a 23-year-old male, presented with a chief complaint of mechanical low back pain that had been present for 8 months. He had a history of falling in the sitting position on two different occasions during his martial arts practice. Initially, his symptoms were localised, infrequent, and aggravated by prolonged sitting. Over the course of six months, he developed sciatica radiating to the dorsum of his left foot and associated with numbness but no weakness. Systemic review was unremarkable, and he had no constitutional symptoms.

After undergoing an MRI, a discal cyst located in the anterior epidural space with low signal intensity on T1-weighted images and high signal intensity on T2-weighted images was discovered. It appeared faintly white in colour, contained serous fluid, and partially indented the L5 nerve root. The patient underwent an endoscopic interlaminar surgery under general anaesthesia, in prone position on Jackson table. The cyst was excised at the base of the connection by performing an annulotomy. A fragment of the cyst wall composed of fibrocartilaginous tissue devoid of epithelial lining was found on histopathological examination.

The patient had immediate relief of his sciatica symptoms and was ambulating well two days after surgery. He was discharged home with no signs of post-operative complications. At ten months post-surgery, there were no signs indicating any recurrence.

Discharge Medications:
N/A

Follow-up Instructions:
The patient is advised to follow up with his medical provider as needed to monitor any recurring symptoms. He should continue to avoid prolonged sitting and take the necessary precautions to prevent any further falls during his martial arts practice.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The condition chiefly responsible for the admission is a lumbar discal cyst compressing the L5 nerve root and causing sciatica, which is an intervertebral disc disorder with radiculopathy. Disc disorders belong to chapter M (musculoskeletal). The category for other intervertebral disc disorders, which covers the lumbar region, is M51.

CODE: M51
